sanskrit: satyenottabhitā bhūmiḥ sūryeṇottabhitā dyauḥ | ṛtenādityās tiṣṭhanti divi somo adhi śritaḥ ||
english: By truth the earth is upheld; by the sun the sky is upheld; by cosmic order (ṛta) the Ādityas stand firm; in heaven Soma is exalted.

sanskrit: somenādityā balinaḥ somena pṛthivī mahī | ato nakṣatraṇām eṣām upasthe soma āhitaḥ ||
english: By Soma the Ādityas are mighty; by Soma the great earth endures; therefore Soma is placed in the lap of these constellations.

sanskrit: somaṃ manyate papivān yat saṃpiṃṣanty oṣadhim | somaṃ yaṃ braḥmāno vidur na tasyāśnāti pārthivaḥ ||
english: One who has drunk thinks he has drunk Soma when they press the plant; the Soma that the brahmins know — of that no earthly being partakes.

sanskrit: ācchadvidhānair gupito bārhataiḥ soma rakṣitaḥ | grāvṇām ic chṛṇvan tiṣṭhasi na te aśnāti pārthivaḥ ||
english: Protected by covering rites, guarded by Bārhaté hymns, O Soma, you stand listening to the pressing-stones; no earthly being eats of you.

sanskrit: cittir vāvopabarhaṇaṃ cakṣur āvad abhyañjanam | dyaur bhūmiḥ kośa āsīd yad ayāt sūryā patim ||
english: Thought was the bridal cushion, sight the anointing; heaven and earth were the casket when Sūryā went to her husband.

sanskrit: raibhy āsīd anudeyī nārāśaṃsī nyocanam | sūryāyā bhadram id vāso gāthayaiti pariṣkṛtā ||
english: The Raibhī verse was the gift-accompanying (bride's) escort; the Nārāśaṃsī was the wooing chant; adorned with the Gāthā song, Sūryā's auspicious garment comes.

sanskrit: stomā āsan pratidhayaḥ kurīraṃ chanda opaśaḥ | sūryāyā aśvinā varā- -agnir āsīt purogavaḥ ||
english: The praise-hymns (stoma) were the bridal supports; the meter was the headdress (kurīra); the Aśvins were Sūryā's suitors; Agni went as the vanguard.

sanskrit: somo vadhūyur abhavad aśvināstām ubhā varā | sūryāṃ yat patye śaṃsantīṃ manasā savitādadāt ||
english: Soma became the wooer of the bride; the Aśvins were both her suitors; when Sūryā was proclaimed in mind as destined for her lord, Savitṛ gave her away.

sanskrit: mano asyā ana āsīd dyaur āsīd uta chadiḥ | śukrāv anaḍvāhāv āstāṃ yad ayāt sūryā patim ||
english: Mind was her chariot-body; heaven was its canopy; two bright bullocks were yoked when Sūryā went to her husband.

sanskrit: ṛksāmābhyām abhihitau gāvau te sāmanāv aitām | śrotre te cakre āstāṃ divi panthāś carācaraḥ ||
english: The two cows driven on by Ṛk and Sāman came as your Sāman-verses; your two wheels were hearing itself; in heaven the path moves ever to and fro.

sanskrit: śucī te cakre yātyā vyāno akṣa āhataḥ | ano manasmayaṃ sūryā- -ārohat prayatī patim ||
english: Your two wheels are pure as you travel; the axle of the wind is driven; Sūryā mounted the mind-made chariot, going forth toward her lord.

sanskrit: sūryāyā vahatuḥ prāgāt savitā yam avāsṛjat | aghāsu hanyante gāvaḥ phalgunīṣu vy uhyate ||
english: The bridal procession of Sūryā moved forward, the one whom Savitṛ released; at the (asterism) Agha cattle are slaughtered; under the Phalgunīs she is carried in procession.

sanskrit: yad aśvinā pṛcchamānāv ayātaṃ tricakreṇa vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ | kvaikaṃ cakraṃ vām āsīt kva deṣṭrāya tasthathuḥ ||
english: When you two Aśvins came questioning, with a three-wheeled vehicle for the bridal procession of Sūryā — where was your one wheel, where did you stand to guide?

sanskrit: yad ayātaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryām upa | viśve devā anu tad vām ajānan putraḥ pitarāv avṛnīta pūṣā ||
english: When you two lords of prosperity came to choose Sūryā as bride, all the gods knew that of yours; Pūṣan chose you as fathers — as a son does.

sanskrit: dve te cakre sūrye brahmāṇa ṛtuthā viduḥ | athaikaṃ cakraṃ yad guhā tad addhātaya id viduḥ ||
english: Your two wheels, O Sūryā, the brahmins know in their proper seasons; but the one wheel that is hidden — only the truly devoted know that.

sanskrit: pra tvā muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśād yena tvābadhnāt savitā suśevāḥ | ṛtasya yonau sukṛtasya loke syonaṃ te astu sahapatnyai vadhu ||
english: I release you from the snare of Varuṇa with which the gracious Savitṛ bound you; in the womb of cosmic order, in the world of the well-performed, may it be easy for you, O bride, together with your husband.

sanskrit: aryamaṇaṃ yajāmahe subandhuṃ pativedanam | urvārukam iva bandhanād ito muñcantu māmutaḥ ||
english: We worship Aryaman, the good kinsman, finder of a husband; may they release me from here and from there, as a cucumber from its stalk.

sanskrit: preto muñcantu māmutaḥ subaddhām amutas karat | yatheyam indra mīḍhvaḥ suputrā subhagāsati ||
english: May they release me from here and from there, may he make her well-bound from that side; so that she, O Indra the bounteous, may be blessed with fine sons and good fortune.

sanskrit: bhagas tveto nayatu hastagṛhya- -aśvinā tvā pra vahatāṃ rathena | gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidatham ā vadāsi ||
english: May Bhaga lead you from here, taking your hand; may the Aśvins carry you forward in their chariot; go to the house, that you may be mistress of the house, a free woman who speaks at the assembly.

sanskrit: iha priyaṃ prajāyai te sam ṛdhyatām asmin gṛhe gārhapatyāya jāgṛhi | enā patyā tanvaṃ saṃ spṛśasva- -atha jirvir vidatham ā vadāsi ||
english: May what is dear to you here prosper for progeny; be wakeful in this house for the gārhapatya (householder's fire); unite your body with this husband; and then as an elder you shall speak at the assembly.

sanskrit: ihaiva staṃ mā vi yauṣṭaṃ dīrgham āyur vy aśnutam | krīḍantau putrair naptṛbhir modamānau sve gṛhe ||
english: Remain here together, be not parted; enjoy a long life; playing with sons and grandsons, rejoicing in your own home.

sanskrit: pūrvāparaṃ carato māyayaitau śiśū krīḍantau pari yāto adhvaram | viśvāny anyo bhuvanā vicaṣṭa ṛtūṃr anyo vidadhaj jāyate navaḥ ||
english: These two youths roam east and west by their power, playing they go around the sacrifice; one surveys all the worlds; the other, assigning the seasons, is born ever new.

sanskrit: navonavo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṃ ketur uṣasām ety agram | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vi dadhāty āyan pra candramās tirate dīrgham āyuḥ ||
english: Born again and again he becomes new, the banner of the days; he goes to the fore of the dawns; apportioning the share to the gods as he comes, the moon extends long life.

sanskrit: parā dehi śāmūlyaṃ brahmabhyo vi bhajā vasu | kṛtyaiṣā padvatī bhūtvā- -ā jāyā viśate patim ||
english: Give away the śāmūlya garment to the brahmins; distribute the goods; this witchcraft, having become a footprint-tracker, enters the wife who enters the husband.

sanskrit: nīlalohitaṃ bhavati kṛtyāsaktir vy ajyate | edhante asyā jñātayaḥ patir bandheṣu badhyate ||
english: It becomes dark-red, the attachment of witchcraft is dissolved; her kinsmen prosper while the husband is bound in fetters.

sanskrit: aślīlā tanūr bhavati ruśatī pāpayāmuyā | patir yad vadhvo vāsasaḥ svam aṅgam abhyūrṇute ||
english: The body becomes inauspicious, afflicted by that evil (charm); when the husband wraps his own limb with the bride's garment.

sanskrit: āśasanaṃ viśasanam atho adhivikartanam | sūryāyāḥ paśya rūpāṇi tāni brahmā tu śundhati ||
english: The tearing away, the cutting apart, and also the further trimming — look upon the forms of Sūryā's (garment); the brahmin purifies these.

sanskrit: tṛṣṭam etat kaṭukam apāṣṭhavad viṣavan naitad attave | sūryāṃ yo brahmā veda sa id vādhūyam arhati ||
english: This is harsh, bitter, hard like a hoof-paring, poisonous — not fit to eat; only that brahmin who knows Sūryā truly deserves to handle the bridal rites.

sanskrit: sa vai tat syonaṃ harati brahmā vāsaḥ sumaṅgalam | prāyaścittiṃ yo adhyeti yena jāyā na riṣyati ||
english: That brahmin carries away the soft, auspicious garment — he who studies the expiation rite by which the wife comes to no harm.

sanskrit: yuvaṃ bhagaṃ saṃ bharathaḥ samṛddham ṛtaṃ vadantām ṛtodyena | brahmaṇaspate patim asyai rocayāmuṃ cāru sambhalo vadatu vācam etām ||
english: You two bring together abundant fortune; let them speak truth, roused by the truth; O Brahmaṇaspati, make this husband shine for her; and let the good provider speak this word beautifully.
